whatItDoes: Change how Haxtun uses its existing 0.5% sales and use tax beginning January 1, 2027. Half of this tax, or 0.25 percentage points, would pay for streets, street repairs and drainage improvements. The other half would continue to fund and maintain the community center, which currently receives the full tax. The existing 0.5% tax rate would stay the same.
yesMeans: Allow half of this existing tax to support the stated street and drainage projects and keep the other half for the community center.
noMeans: Do not approve this reallocation of the community-center tax.

whatItDoes: Continue Holyoke’s existing 2.5% lodging tax for six more years, through December 31, 2032, instead of letting it expire on December 31, 2026. The tax applies to rooms and other accommodations in commercial lodging facilities rented or leased by short-term visitors and guests. Revenue would continue to pay for the city’s recreation programs at the same tax rate.
yesMeans: Extend the existing lodging tax for city recreation programs through the end of 2032 at its current rate.
noMeans: Do not extend this tax beyond its scheduled expiration through this question.
